name: ssh-image-drop
title: SSH Image Drop
description: Send files, folders, and clipboard images over SSH with a single hotkey, and pull them back — no path typing, the remote path lands on your clipboard. Handy for handing screenshots to remote Claude Code / CLI sessions that can't take an image paste. Passwords are stored in the system credential store (macOS Keychain / Windows DPAPI) by default; SSH key auth is optional.
author: wjsong

commands.name: send-file-to-server
commands.title: Send File to Server
commands.description: Send files or folders to a server with a picker form (pre-filled from your Finder selection on macOS), or pick a server for clipboard and pull transfers

commands.name: send-clipboard-image
commands.title: Send Clipboard Image
commands.description: Send the clipboard image over SSH and copy the remote path

commands.name: pull-file
commands.title: Pull File from Server
commands.description: Download the remote file or folder whose path is in the clipboard, reveal it in the file manager, and copy the local path

commands.name: add-server
commands.title: Manage Servers
commands.description: Add, edit, or delete servers; passwords are stored in the system credential store by default (optional SSH key install)

preferences.name: remoteDir
preferences.title: Remote Directory
preferences.description: Directory on the server where uploaded files are stored (cleared on reboot when under /tmp)

preferences.name: hideConfigHosts
preferences.title: Server List
preferences.label: Hide ~/.ssh/config servers
preferences.description: Show only managed and recently used servers (your ~/.ssh/config is not modified)

preferences.name: pasteTargetApp
preferences.title: Auto-Paste
preferences.description: App that receives the remote path after Send Clipboard Image — pasted only if that app is frontmost when the transfer finishes, into whichever field has focus there. Leave unset to only copy the path. File sends and pulls always copy only
